text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Culturally safe, trauma-informed care: address her as Liliʻuokalani, as she asked; take time; explain each test and treatment plainly before it is done; involve her ʻohana as she chooses while she makes the decisions; acknowledge the history of the overthrow when she raises it, without probing
  • Same-day emergency stroke evaluation today (CT, CT angiography of the head and neck, swallow screen and laboratory tests), then vascular neurology consultation at the rapid-access stroke clinic tomorrow morning, with diffusion MRI and an echocardiogram
  • Dual antiplatelet therapy started within 24 hours of onset once CT excluded bleeding: aspirin 325 mg and clopidogrel 300 mg loading doses, then aspirin 81 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg daily for 21 days, then a single antiplatelet; stop antiplatelets if anticoagulation is started
  • Atorvastatin 40 mg daily, a high-intensity statin, with a lipid panel at four to twelve weeks; LDL goal below 70 mg/dL
  • Bedside swallow screen before any food or drink, a cognition screen (MoCA) at the stroke clinic, a depression screen, and a falls assessment
  • BE FAST: balance, eyes, face, arm, speech, time to call 911; call 911 at once for any new symptom, even if it passes, and do not drive herself
  • Native Hawaiian healing alongside clinic care, if she wishes: lomilomi through Ke Ola Mamo, a Native Hawaiian Health Care System, with the practitioner told that she takes blood thinners, and hoʻoponopono with her ʻohana as they choose; the clinic asks nothing further about her practices
  • Blood pressure: home readings twice daily for a week; if the average is 130/80 mmHg or higher after the first week, start losartan 25 mg daily, with potassium and creatinine two weeks later; target below 130/80 mmHg
  • Rhythm monitoring for atrial fibrillation for 30 days with an ambulatory patch, because the stroke is embolic in pattern; if atrial fibrillation is found, stop antiplatelets and start a direct oral anticoagulant
  • Apixaban 5 mg twice daily for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (CHA2DS2-VASc 6, HAS-BLED 2), with clopidogrel stopped; blood count and kidney function before starting and about every five to six months at her age and kidney function; bleeding precautions, no anti-inflammatory pain medicines, and a falls plan
  • Laboratory tests drawn at clinic visits, or at home by the clinic's nurse, instead of separate trips to the laboratory
  • Daily walking, the foods she already eats with less salted and preserved food, alcohol kept to rare occasions, and no smoking

resource.title: Liliʻuokalani synthetic care plan
resource.description: A minor ischemic stroke presenting as a transient ischemic attack in a 78-year-old Native Hawaiian elder, composer and community leader in Honolulu. The episode covers same-day evaluation of transient weakness and speech difficulty (ABCD2 score, CT and CT angiography of the head and neck, then diffusion MRI the next morning, which turns a suspected TIA into a minor stroke); a 21-day course of aspirin and clopidogrel started within 24 hours, as in POINT and CHANCE; ECG, echocardiogram and 30-day rhythm monitoring that find paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and the change from antiplatelets to apixaban with correct dosing; a high-intensity statin to an LDL below 70 mg/dL; a blood pressure target below 130/80 mmHg; swallow, cognition, mood and falls screening; a nosebleed on apixaban; all under the 2021 AHA/ASA secondary stroke prevention guideline and the CMID stroke and atrial fibrillation monographs. It also teaches culturally safe care: asking how she wishes to be addressed, involving her ʻohana as she chooses, offering Native Hawaiian healing such as lomilomi and hoʻoponopono alongside Western care without probing or describing practices, and acknowledging the historical trauma of the overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom, which the United States formally apologized for in 1993.
